### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: two, answered here — (1) where the `Tier:` spelling should live for the seat that WRITES the brief, the references-tier ratchet having zero headroom: the seat answers A for now (the H65 remedy text is the spelling's home; the triage seat has been told on #18302's ACCEPT) and takes the dev's B/C recommendation to the maintainer as a one-line ask — raise the `dispatch-runbook.md` ceiling by one, or name a redundant runbook line to pay — the seat does not delete a runbook rule on its own judgment; (2) whether the bought window should walk back a page when the newest page holds no artefact: A — the newest page held 16 comments / 9 artefacts across five days, the clause declares the residual, and B is a cheap follow-up only if the seat's comment rate rises. Three seat premises the dev refuted, owned here: (1) 「H99 is the highest id」 — H64 is; H99 is the self-test's deliberate unregistered code, so H65 is the next free id; (2) 「read the window the patrol already uses」 — that window is the thread's FIRST page (the endpoint serves oldest-first and ignores `direction`/`sort`, measured), five weeks stale on #6015, so a row on it could never see a live round; (3) 「PR #18276 still in the queue」 — it had landed; the branch is cut from `53dd5aaa`. Five deviations answered: ① the row BUYS the newest page (`ceil(comments/100)`, one request per triage post per run, judged in place, never written to `commentCache`) — accepted, the ruling's intent and still one predicate over the board; the seat re-read the placement comment and the no-cache clause; ② no runbook line — accepted: `dispatch-runbook.md` 241/241 and SKILL.md 812/812 have zero headroom, a deletion there is a protocol change outside the card, a ceiling raise needs a maintainer ruling; the remedy text is the spelling's only home until the seat pays a line or the maintainer rules; ③ one row per carrier naming the newest — accepted; ④ the `typeof null` wrapper spelling in the cases — accepted; ⑤ a real stamp in the remedy example (the platform eats angle-bracket fragments in bodies) — accepted. Out of scope, FILED by the seat: H44's seat leg is blind on the triage post (first-page corpus + a regex that no longer matches the marker spelling), H56 / H64 share the corpus. Noted for the maintainer: both rules-layer files sit at their ceilings.
